Someone with zero running history should start with walk/jog (or walking), not continuous running.
No harder running sessions in the first month for a complete beginner.

Equipment is bodyweight only; the repertoire must stay within it.

expectations.rationale: The race week stays in place after the last pre-race review.
The race stays prescribed on its date.
A short taper suits a novice 10K.
expectations.statement: Running in the final 7-10 days before the race is reduced relative to the peak weeks, with no new or harder session types introduced in race week, and strength in race week is light or absent in the two days before the race.

DUPLICATE_SECOND_SOURCE.desc: Each completed report also arrives from a second device with the same values

RENAME_OPAQUE_IDS.desc: Athlete, event, report and activity ids and provider names renamed

LOAD_CONVENTION_EQUIVALENT.desc: A known dumbbell-pair load given PER_HAND instead of TOTAL (or the reverse), same mass

RESEND.desc: Every decision re-sends the previous decision's reports (same ids)

CARRIER_CLINICAL.desc: An answer to UNREPORTED_TRAINING recorded by a clinical substitution, then qualified clearance; compared at the first eligible decision

CARRIER_HOLD.desc: An answer in the program's last week recorded by a refused schedule change (HOLD); compared at the next decision

RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK.desc: A stated break its own decision did not apply, stated again with every later review that states none until a return is recorded: identical decisions (no repetition is ever needed)

INSERT_NEWER_BREAK.desc: A review that applied a return reading a kept break, sent again with a newer break that names none: its relation is unresolved, so no return is applied and the plan is not valid (no last-write-wins, no join)

expectations.rationale: Complete in-scope intake.
Strength-first hybrid.
expectations.statement: Strength carries the hypertrophy goal (three sessions, moderate reps, known loads in their own conventions, reps in reserve about 1-3, gradual volume progression); running is easy, modest and progresses slowly from 70 minutes per week.

expectations.rationale: Noise is not a reason to ask or hold.
A "too easy" report is not a clinical or missing-fact situation.
Without consent the coach does not learn.
expectations.statement: With learning consent off, no personal response pattern is stored or applied; any change after the second "too easy" report is the ordinary per-decision response for that session (for example a normal load or rep step), not a learned faster progression for the athlete.

expectations.rationale: A marathon is outside V1; the request is not planned.
No race is added to the plan in force.
An out-of-scope request does not replace the plan.
expectations.statement: The plan in force after the request is the previous hypertrophy/general plan, not a marathon build.

expectations.rationale: Training continues normally after the rejected request.

expectations.rationale: Complete intake with a partial history.
Use partial data honestly.
expectations.statement: The partial history is read as about three runs a week (about 135-150 minutes, long run near 70 minutes) and one light strength session; UTC-stamped rows are attributed to their local dates; the starting week is near that level, neither from zero nor above it.

expectations.rationale: All sessions are reported.
De-duplication and local-date attribution.
expectations.statement: The phone and watch reports of the Sunday long run are one session (counted once) and the long run is dated on Sunday local time, not Saturday.

expectations.rationale: Correction within the same decision.
expectations.statement: The 95-minute typo is superseded by its correction: it is not treated as an overperformance and does not drive any progression; arrival order does not matter.

expectations.rationale: A correction changes the future plan, never what was already decided or done.
expectations.statement: After the late correction, the plan from week 4 treats the week-2 long run as done (no remedial or reduced long run because of a miss that did not happen), while the week-3 decisions already taken are not rewritten.

expectations.rationale: A report stamped two days after the decision time cannot be used as given.
Only reported facts with valid times write history.
expectations.statement: The future-stamped long run is not written to the completed-work record as given (not dated in week 5, not counted as done in week 4 until its time is resolved).

expectations.rationale: The re-synced report resolves the hold.
Nothing pending.

expectations.rationale: Honouring the chosen days with light sessions is preferred; asking about capacity is acceptable.
Capacity, not availability, sets the dose.
expectations.statement: Week-0 total running is close to current capacity (roughly 30-70 minutes spread over the six days as walks, walk/jog, very short easy runs or rest by design), not six 30-minute runs plus a 60-minute long run.

expectations.rationale: No harder running for a novice in a 4-week general program.
Equipment and turns.
expectations.statement: Strength uses only bodyweight and bands; on shared days running is AM and strength PM.

expectations.rationale: Everything is reported.
No session of week 0 is unknown.
Mixed execution with two shortened/hard runs.
expectations.statement: Week 1 does not increase running over week 0; it holds or reduces, and does not schedule make-up sessions for the two missed runs.

expectations.rationale: An empty review leaves all week-1 runs unknown.
The question lists the unreported runs.
Nothing prescribed while the question stands.
Four runs are still unknown after the partial answer.
Still pending.
All week-1 runs are now known.
Nothing pending (strength unknowns do not block run doses).
Plan for what the athlete does.
expectations.statement: Week 2 running is not above week 1's planned load; the plan adapts toward the two to three sessions he actually does (lighter content on the other chosen days), without catch-up.

VARIANT.desc: The author's own variant and expected relation

expectations.rationale: A healthy older adult is in scope.
No running for a strength-only athlete with no run days.
A true beginner at 63.
expectations.statement: Two full-body sessions of simple machine/dumbbell/bodyweight exercises covering the main patterns, ESTABLISH loads (no guessed numbers), low volume (about 1-3 sets) and reps in reserve of about 3 or more at first, progressing slowly; only machines, dumbbells, bench or bodyweight are used.

expectations.rationale: First logged loads become the reference only after confirmation.
expectations.statement: The first logged loads are presented for confirmation and are not used to raise the loads before they are confirmed.

expectations.rationale: General fatigue from poor sleep is not a clinical signal.
Respond to systemic fatigue.
expectations.statement: The Monday session is eased (fewer sets or more reps in reserve, or shortened) and nothing progresses that day.

expectations.rationale: Unanswered eligibility is a question; it is never a clearance and never a presumed illness.
Nothing is prescribed until eligibility is answered.
Eligibility answered with nothing clinical; the re-sent week is counted once.
Nothing pending.
Single adverse strength response.
expectations.statement: After the adverse Thursday response, the next week does not increase lower-body load or volume; a small reduction or a repeat is appropriate, and there is no clinical route (no pain was reported).

expectations.rationale: Complete in-scope intake.
Two and a half weeks of planned runs have no report.
The question is about the unreported runs.
Nothing prescribed while the question stands.
A 17-day break calls for a re-plan.
The declared break covers the unknown sessions.
No hard running in the first days back.
The first full week back does not exceed the last pre-break long run.
Schedule change and no catch-up.
expectations.statement: From the change on, runs are scheduled in the PM turn on days 1, 3 and 5; nothing is added to make up for the break.

expectations.rationale: Return after five weeks off.
Fully declared nonclinical break.
The first week after a long break is a return week.
No hard running in the return week.
The return long run is shorter than the last pre-break long run.
Detraining after five weeks.
expectations.statement: Return running is roughly 40-60% of the week-8 level, anchored on the 20-minute demonstration; strength resumes at reduced loads or volume (for example re-established or about 10-20% below the last logged loads) with more reserve.
